newsitem.title: Russia: Russian parliament demands Ukraine surrender port.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament demands Ukraine surrender port.

text.p: The upper chamber of the Russian parliament on Thursday publicly demanded that Ukraine hand over the Black Sea naval port of Sevastopol, saying it was part of Russia and Kiev had no right to govern it.
The Federation Council, in a move likely to cause a storm of protest in Kiev and disrupt delicate negotiations between the two governments, endorsed the claim by a majority of 110 to 14.

"Unilateral actions by the Ukrainian side aimed at tearing away from Russia a part of its territory (Sevastopol) are not only illegal under international law, but also directly damage Russia's security," the resolution said.

Ukraine's actions "are preventing the establishment of good neighbourly and profitable relations between two fraternal peoples and are lowering the authority of both countries in the international arena", it said.
The resolution and another document setting up a special commission to prepare a draft law on the status of Sevastopol, are not binding on President Boris Yeltsin or the government.
The Kremlin ruled Ukraine for more than three centuries, but it recognised Ukrainian territorial integrity at the time of the breakup of the Soviet Union in 1991.
Russia and Ukraine have failed to agree in more than four years of negotiation what to do about the disputed former Soviet Black Sea fleet, based mainly in Sevastopol.
The two governments have been discussing a lease agreement under which Russia would keep most of the fleet and continue to use Sevastopol as a base.
But talks have foundered over Russian demands that the Ukrainian navy should base itself elsewhere, a demand which Kiev has rejected as interference in its internal affairs.
Both documents approved by the Federation Council on Thursday were proposed by Moscow's powerful mayor Yuri Luzhkov, a Yeltsin ally who is widely touted as a possible successor to the president.
He argued that a 1954 Kremlin decision to transfer the Crimean peninsula from Russia to Ukraine did not include Sevastopol which had a special status at the time.

The second document passed by the Council expressed "concern that the Ukrainian side, against the norm of international law and existing agreements, insists in its refusal to accept the Russian status of Sevastopol".

Yeltsin has promised to visit Kiev to sign a friendship treaty with President Leonid Kuchma, but has insisted that the Ukrainian and Russian prime ministers first sign an agreement on the Black Sea Fleet.
In a Russian television interview last Saturday Kuchma suggested going ahead with the treaty and settling the Fleet issue later, but a Kremlin spokesman rejected this option.
Kuchma also floated the idea of reverting to a joint command of the Fleet, first agreed in 1992 but later abandoned in favour of dividing it between the two states.
The Federation Council vote followed an earlier resolution several weeks ago on Sevastopol by the lower house, the State Duma, which infuriated Ukraine's parliament and government.
Kuchma met Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin in Lisbon earlier this week but officials said they were unable to break the stalemate over Sevastopol and the fleet.
